channel.title: Crypto Record
channel.description: Crypto Record reports news on Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, DeFi protocols, exchanges, stablecoins, regulation and network upgrades across the crypto market.

item.title: What a Cross-Chain Bridge Quote Leaves Out
item.description: A bridge quote combines network gas, bridge fees and swap costs in different ways. Learn what to check before signing and how to compare routes fairly.

item.title: What an Intermediate Asset Means in a Treasury Route
item.description: A cross-chain treasury route may pass through an asset it never meant to hold; trace each leg, token form and accounting role before judging the result.

item.title: When Splitting a Cross-Chain Swap Pays
item.description: Splitting a cross-chain swap can improve the received amount when routes have different marginal costs, but extra fees and delay can erase the gain.

item.title: Why BSC Pair Choice Comes Down to Liquidity or Recency
item.description: On BSC, choose a trading pair by matching pool depth to your trade, then use recency to judge whether its price and activity still reflect current demand.

item.title: Why BSC Swap Quotes Change With Trade Size
item.description: A BSC swap quote changes with trade size because larger trades consume more pool reserves, increasing price impact alongside fees and any routing costs.

item.title: Mantle withdrawals: fast inclusion, slower Ethereum settlement
item.description: Mantle withdrawals can appear on the rollup quickly, while Ethereum settlement waits for proof, a challenge window and a final claim; that shapes when funds are usable.

item.title: What Token Allowlisting Means for L2 Integrators
item.description: An L2 token allowlist controls what a route accepts; token support covers the wider work needed to quote, display, transfer and account for that asset.

item.title: How to Check Whether a Mantle Bridge Transfer Arrived
item.description: A Mantle transfer is complete only when the destination chain records it; follow the bridge status and transaction hash to distinguish arrival from a pending relay.

item.title: Why Mantle Bridge Transfers Stay Pending
item.description: A pending Mantle Bridge transfer may be awaiting Ethereum confirmation, proof or a separate claim; the direction tells you which step comes next.

item.title: Reconcile Every Treasury Bridge Transfer
item.description: A clean bridge close matches the source debit to the destination credit, accounts for fees and timing, and leaves an auditable record for every transfer.

item.title: When Is a Treasury Bridge Transfer Final?
item.description: A treasury bridge transfer is complete only when the destination asset is usable and reconciled; source confirmations, bridge messages and exit stages set that point.

item.title: How Much ETH Should You Keep for Manta Pacific Gas?
item.description: Keep enough ETH on Manta Pacific for the next transaction and a buffer; the right reserve depends on what you plan to do and the fee shown at the time.

item.title: Why a Native Crypto Swap Takes Time
item.description: A native swap waits on source-chain confirmation, validator witnessing, execution by the swap protocol and a destination-chain payout, so the slowest leg sets the pace.

item.title: What a Chainflip Swap Estimate Actually Tells You
item.description: A swap estimate combines a live price, route costs and expected payout; reading each figure separately shows what may change before your assets arrive.

item.title: What a minimum does in a wallet swap
item.description: A swap minimum sets the least output your wallet will accept; see how quotes, slippage and execution rules shape an on-chain trade and when it will fail.

item.title: What Historical Pool Volume Says About Fee Potential
item.description: Historical volume estimates a pool’s gross fees only when paired with its fee rate; liquidity depth and fee sharing shape what providers receive after trading costs.

item.title: What One Solana Swap Actually Costs
item.description: A Solana swap can cost more than its network fee: the route may add pool fees, price impact and temporary account funding, each working differently.

item.title: Byreal: Choose a Swap or Concentrated Liquidity?
item.description: Byreal supports token swaps and concentrated liquidity on Solana; choose a swap for a trade, or provide liquidity only if you can manage a price range.

item.title: How to Route Treasury Transfers Through an Intermediate Chain
item.description: An intermediate chain can make a treasury transfer possible when no direct route exists, but each hop adds fees, settlement time and another point to reconcile.

item.title: Who Gets DEX Fees When Liquidity Is Staked in a Gauge
item.description: Gauge staking usually directs token emissions to liquidity providers; swap fees follow the pool’s own rules, which may pay LPs, voters, or both after each trade.
